clue.text: Change to reverse for hilly road

parts.note: to change is to switch
to reverse is to back, as a car backs up

explanation.surface: Someone advises turning round to avoid a road over the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: A switchback is a road or track that climbs and dips, or zigzags up a steep slope.

clue.text: Marvellous exercise, to run through boat

indicators.note: through means the boat's word is pierced by the other letters running through its middle

parts.note: sub is short for submarine
PE is physical education
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A rower thinks running through a boat is great exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb means excellent or magnificent.

clue.text: Surge to get popular water-plant

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a rush is a marsh plant growing by water

explanation.surface: A trendy aquatic plant sees a boom in sales.
explanation.definitionFit: An inrush is a sudden flooding in, like a surge of water.

clue.text: Complaining over service — that's liable to cause chain reaction

definitions.text: that's liable to cause chain reaction

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: critical means fault-finding or complaining
mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A grumble about a church service sets off a string of events.
explanation.definitionFit: In nuclear physics this is the minimum amount of fissile material needed to sustain a self-propagating reaction.

clue.text: City club home at first

parts.note: a bat is a club used in sports such as cricket

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word home

explanation.surface: A city's club plays its opening match at home.
explanation.walkthrough: BATH is a Roman spa city in Somerset, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath is an English city famous for its Roman baths and Georgian architecture.

clue.text: Astonished to find criminal established

parts.note: con is short for convict, a criminal
founded means set up or established

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed to discover a crook started the firm.
explanation.definitionFit: To be confounded is to be bewildered or amazed.

clue.text: Almost rope in young woman

indicators.note: almost means the word for rope stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: a lasso is a rope with a noose for catching cattle

explanation.surface: A cowboy nearly ropes in a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Lass is a Scottish and northern English word for a girl.

clue.text: Staunch a wound made by prickly plant

indicators.note: wound, read as the past tense of wind, says the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A first-aider stems bleeding from a cut caused by a thorny plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like an injury but is the past tense of wind, twisting the letters of STAUNCH A.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus is a spiny-leaved plant, its leaves the model for Corinthian column carving.

clue.text: Mass movement at a fearfully fast tempo

definitions.text: Mass movement at a fearfully fast tempo

parts.words: Mass movement at a fearfully fast tempo
parts.note: sounds like a section of a choral Mass played quickly, but describes panicked animals or crowds fleeing together

explanation.definitionFit: A herd or crowd rushing headlong in panic is this kind of sudden flight.

clue.text: Long-lasting prettiness is remarkable

indicators.note: remarkable can mean re-marked, so the letters of prettiness are set down again in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone praises a beauty that endures.
explanation.definitionFit: Something persistent continues for a long time without stopping.

clue.text: Airline repeatedly supplying cake

indicators.note: repeatedly says the airline's initials appear twice in a row

parts.note: BA is British Airways, the UK flag carrier

explanation.surface: A flight serves cake again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: A baba is a small rum-soaked sponge, a rich yeast pastry.

clue.text: Collision on top of stairs, damaging end of flight

indicators.note: in a down clue on top of places the first piece above the second

parts.note: a crash is a collision
a landing is the level area at the head of a staircase

explanation.surface: Someone falls at the head of the stairs and hurts themselves at the end of the flight.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's flight is of stairs; the definition's flight is in an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft coming down hard and being wrecked on touchdown makes this emergency arrival.

clue.text: One hastening to speak for the country

indicators.note: to speak signals that the word for one hastening is said out loud, giving a near-identical sound

parts.note: one who hastens is a rusher

explanation.surface: Someone hurries to act as the nation's spokesperson.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent RUSHER and RUSSIA sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia is a nation spanning eastern Europe and northern Asia.

clue.text: At home, pester for a slice of bread

definitions.meaning: to pester someone at their own front entrance, as reporters do to people in the news
a very thick slab cut from a loaf

explanation.definitionFit: Journalists hounding someone outside their house are said to do this; the same word is slang for a chunky hunk cut from a loaf.

clue.text: Write to city, to take part in small speculative investment

parts.note: to pen is to write
NY is New York
to share is to take part in something

explanation.surface: An investor writes to New York to get in on a small gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: These are low-priced stocks, bought cheaply in the hope of large gains.

clue.text: O, Ann dead? Fuss is wrong, if she's this

indicators.note: is wrong says the letters of the preceding words are not in their correct order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A worried friend asks whether Ann has died, and is told the panic is mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is wrong' rearranges the twelve letters of O, ANN, DEAD and FUSS; if the fuss is misplaced, Ann is unharmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unharmed and in no danger is described with this idiom of well-being.

clue.text: Chief looked to be squinting

parts.note: a boss is a chief
eyed means looked at

explanation.surface: The head of the firm appears to be peering narrowly.
explanation.definitionFit: Boss-eyed is British slang for cross-eyed or having a squint.

clue.text: Remembered being led clear after disaster

indicators.note: after disaster means the letters of led clear are thrown into chaos

explanation.surface: A survivor recalls being guided to safety after a catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: To have recalled something is to have brought it back to mind.

clue.text: Without prejudice, objected to being publicly surrounded

indicators.note: being surrounded means the word for publicly goes around the word for objected

parts.note: done publicly is done openly
if you minded something, you objected to it

explanation.surface: Someone resents being crowded in on in public.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge without prejudice is to keep an unbiased, receptive attitude.

clue.text: A master taking vessel over this canal?

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the vessel above the rest

parts.note: a pan is a cooking vessel
MA is Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A captain steers his ship across a famous waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is a link; the question mark admits that the canal hints at ships, while the definition is the country's name used for its canal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Panama Canal crosses the isthmus linking the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.

clue.text: Darn it! The French do interrupt!

parts.note: heck is a mild oath like darn it
le is the French for the

explanation.surface: An exasperated speaker begs French listeners to stop interrupting.
explanation.definitionFit: To heckle is to interrupt a speaker with jeers or taunts.

clue.text: Most scattered to trespass criminally

indicators.note: criminally suggests the letters of trespass are treated wrongly and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A gang of trespassers spreads out across private land.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse means thinly spread, so the superlative is the most thinly distributed.

clue.text: At home, fit to enjoy cigarette so?

parts.note: in is a common word for at home
hale means healthy and fit, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: A healthy person at home wonders whether to light up.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as an example: a smoker draws the smoke into the lungs.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathing in deeply is how a smoker takes in tobacco smoke.

clue.text: Over island, good walking style

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the letter for good above the island

parts.note: an ait is a small island in a river, especially the Thames

explanation.surface: Someone crossing an island has a fine stride.
explanation.definitionFit: Gait is a manner of walking.

clue.text: One soldiers may attack is yellow

definitions.meaning: soldiers are strips of toast dipped into a soft-boiled egg's centre, a British breakfast custom
the yellow part of an egg

explanation.surface: A cowardly target awaits the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Toast fingers called soldiers are dunked in this; it is also the egg's golden centre.

clue.text: Drive through here to see the big game

definitions.text: Drive through here to see the big game

parts.words: Drive through here to see the big game
parts.note: reads like directions to a football stadium, but describes a zoo-like reserve where visitors drive past large wild animals

explanation.definitionFit: Visitors tour such a reserve by car to watch lions and other large wildlife.

clue.text: Double act now no longer seen

indicators.note: double means the word for act is written twice

parts.note: do means act, as in do the right thing

explanation.surface: A comedy duo has stopped performing.
explanation.definitionFit: This flightless bird of Mauritius is extinct, so it is never seen alive any more.

clue.text: Coin I rank by scale

parts.note: a cent is a small coin
a grade is a rank or level

explanation.surface: A collector ranks coins by a measuring system.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Celsius temperature scale, with a hundred degrees between freezing and boiling.
